questions: What exactly constitutes a "full house" in this context - is it three cards of one value and two cards of another value?
Can we choose the same card more than once, or must we select five distinct cards from the seven available?
Are the cards with the same number considered identical, or do we treat each card as unique regardless of their values?
If there are multiple ways to form a full house, does that still count as "Yes" or do we need to check all possibilities?
What should be the output format if the input contains fewer than 7 integers or non-integer values?
How should we handle the case where all seven cards have the same value - can we still form a valid full house?
Is there a specific order or method required for selecting the five cards, or can we choose any combination?
What happens if some A_i values are outside the stated range of 1-13 - should we validate the input or assume it's always correct?

A full house means there are three cards with the same integer x and two cards with another integer y, where x ≠ y. Determine whether it is possible to choose five of them so that the chosen cards form a full house. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: A_1 A_2 A_3 A_4 A_5 A_6 A_7 Output If a full house can be formed by choosing five cards, print Yes; otherwise, print No. Constraints - A_i is an integer between 1 and 13, inclusive.
